Moving in the Bay Area

How much do movers cost Bay Area households?

Enter both ZIP codes in the calculator below to see how much do movers cost Bay Area households for your home, from San Francisco to San Jose.

Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

Plan on $150–$225 an hour for a 3-person crew with a truck, and $720–$1,800 in all, for a 2-bedroom home moved 10 road miles on an off-peak date with no stairs or add-ons. That is the national baseline for how much do movers cost Bay Area households. San Francisco hills, bridge crossings, curb space and California's estimate rules decide how far above it your own move lands.

Crew rates and hours: how much do movers cost Bay Area households?

Inside the Bay Area, nearly every move is billed by the hour, for the crew and the truck together. Each mover adds $50–$75 an hour to the rate, so the crew size sets the rate and the job sets the hours. A studio or 1-bedroom usually takes 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour, and a 3-bedroom house 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour. That is how much do movers cost Bay Area residents before the clock starts, and the hours are where Bay Area moves differ from the rest of the country.

Those rates come from the national rate table behind the calculator, not from Bay Area quotes. Local movers' own price guides often publish higher hourly rates than these, so treat the calculator's range as the yardstick to hold written estimates against, not as a price list for the region.

California's 100-mile line

California's Bureau of Household Goods and Services (BHGS) licenses movers working within the state and enforces the Maximum Rate Tariff, known as Max 4. Its consumer guide draws a line at 100 miles: a move within California of less than 100 miles can be charged by the hour, and a move over 100 miles must be charged by weight and mileage. That line decides how much do movers cost Bay Area households heading out of the region.

Almost any move between Bay Area cities stays under the line. San Francisco to San Jose, Oakland to Palo Alto or Berkeley to Walnut Creek is an hourly job, so traffic and distance show up on the bill as hours. A move down to Southern California crosses the line, and the mover weighs the shipment and prices the miles instead.

San Francisco stairs, hills and curb space

Stairs and steep blocks

Much of San Francisco's housing is flats in older buildings: Victorians and Edwardians with a flight of front steps, narrow inside stairs and no elevator. Add a steep block where the truck parks downhill from the door, and every load takes longer. The calculator asks about stairs and adds crew time for them, and long carries are a charge many Bay Area estimates list on their own, so describe the walk from your door to the curb when you ask for an estimate. A top-floor flat on a hill is where how much do movers cost Bay Area renters climbs fastest.

Reserving the curb

Parking is the other San Francisco variable. The SFMTA issues temporary tow-away No Parking signs for moving vans. You apply through its online portal or by calling 311, and it asks for at least 5 business days between your application and the first day of enforcement. On unmetered streets the signs must go up at least 72 hours before the move, and on metered streets at least 24 hours before. Staff set the fee after inspecting the space, and metered spaces add a charge for each meter for each day.

  • Reserved times must start no earlier than 7 a.m. and end by 10 p.m.
  • The signs don't override street cleaning, red curbs or other posted rules, so check the block first.
  • A moving container on the street needs a separate permit from San Francisco Public Works, not the SFMTA.

Weigh the sign fee against the time a crew loses walking every box from a space around the corner, which also raises how much do movers cost Bay Area households on the day. Oakland, San Jose and the other cities set their own curb rules, so ask the city at your other address too.

Crossing the bay with a loaded truck

Many Bay Area moves cross water. San Francisco to the East Bay means the Bay Bridge, Marin means the Golden Gate, and the Peninsula to the East Bay means the San Mateo or Dumbarton bridge. Each crossing adds drive time that an hourly mover bills, and a backup at the toll plaza adds more. The bay's bridges collect tolls in one direction only, so ask each mover whether the toll is part of its rate or billed to you on top.

Distance between Bay Area cities adds up quickly, too. San Francisco to San Jose is about 50 road miles, so the 10-mile baseline undercounts many moves here. Enter both ZIP codes so the calculator prices the real drive: how much do movers cost Bay Area households moving from one end of the region to the other rises with every extra mile and the crew time that comes with it.

How much do movers cost Bay Area renters for a 2-bedroom flat?

Say you're moving a 2-bedroom flat in the Mission to a 2-bedroom apartment in Oakland. On baseline terms, that move runs $720–$1,800, with a crew of 3 working somewhere between four and a half and eight hours. Real Bay Area conditions then push how much do movers cost Bay Area renters for this flat above the baseline:

  • the flat is up a flight of front steps, and the Oakland building's elevator has to be booked;
  • the Mission street needs SFMTA signs, or the crew carries every load from down the block;
  • the Bay Bridge crossing adds billed drive time, and more at rush hour;
  • a packing service for 2 bedrooms adds $500–$1,200.

Put the real date, stairs and both ZIP codes into the calculator above, and the range moves with each one. Then compare it with the Not to Exceed Price on each mover's agreement.

Your Not to Exceed Price and change orders

California puts the ceiling on how much do movers cost Bay Area households in writing. Under the BHGS guide, a mover pricing a move within the state must make a visual inspection of what you're moving for the estimate, and must sign the estimate. At least three days before the move, the mover must give you the moving agreement, or bill of lading, and you both sign it before moving starts. For a move within California, it should show a Not to Exceed Price: the most you can be charged unless there are change orders. Don't let the crew start until you have that agreement and accept the charges.

A change order is how the price can grow. If you add items after the inspection, you and the mover sign a change order before the shipment is loaded. Keep the inventory complete at the inspection, and how much do movers cost Bay Area households on moving day stays at or under the figure you signed. BHGS also warns about estimates given before an inspection, estimates far cheaper than the rest, estimates missing inventory details, and a business address that is only a P.O. box.

Smaller moves and doing part of it yourself

Not every Bay Area move is a whole home. Moving 4 to 10 pieces, such as a bedroom set and a sofa, typically costs $330–$890 for 10 miles off peak, with no stairs or extras. For a full home, packing your own boxes saves the crew's packing charge, and the box estimator below counts what you'll need. Renting a truck costs least on paper, though in San Francisco you also take on the hills, the parking and the signs. So the answer to how much do movers cost Bay Area households who share the work comes down to which jobs you hand over.

Turning a Bay Area range into a real number

An online range tells you what a move like yours usually costs, and a real number comes from a signed agreement. To get from one to the other:

  1. Run your ZIP codes, home size, date and stairs through the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see the price.
  2. Check each mover's license with BHGS before you book.
  3. Get two or three estimates after a visual inspection, in person if you can, for the same inventory and date.
  4. Compare how each bills travel time, long carries, stairs, packing and bridge tolls.
  5. Read the Not to Exceed Price on the agreement you receive at least three days before the move.

Once that agreement is signed, how much do movers cost Bay Area households stops being a range on a screen and becomes a ceiling written into your contract.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • Within California, a move under 100 miles can be billed by the hour, and a longer one is priced by weight and mileage.
  • Your moving agreement must reach you at least three days before the move, with a Not to Exceed Price on it.
  • San Francisco's moving-day parking signs take at least 5 business days to arrange and go up 72 hours ahead on unmetered streets.
  • Front steps, steep blocks and bridge crossings all add billed time to a Bay Area move.

Tipping movers who hauled up San Francisco hills

A tip isn't part of how much do movers cost Bay Area households on the bill or in the calculator's range, but most guides suggest one. Work out a tip for each mover and for the whole crew, by the hour or by the day.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Questions

How much do movers cost Bay Area households? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

Is moving in Oakland cheaper than in San Francisco?

The hourly rate depends more on the mover than the city, but an Oakland or East Bay move often takes fewer hours: more driveways, easier parking and fewer steep blocks. A San Francisco flat with front steps and no curb space takes longer, so how much do movers cost Bay Area renters tends to be higher in the city even at the same rate. Enter both addresses in the calculator to compare.

How much do movers cost Bay Area households moving more than 100 miles?

Within California, a move of over 100 miles must be charged by weight and mileage, not by the hour, so the size of the load and the distance set the price. For scale, a 1-bedroom home moved 1,000 road miles typically costs $1,400–$3,300 off peak, with no stairs or extras, about $1.45–$3.28 per mile. Enter both ZIP codes for a range on your own route.

Should you pay a large deposit to a Bay Area mover?

Be careful. BHGS tells consumers to be wary of companies that ask for a large deposit, or a deposit by electronic or digital transfer, and to get a receipt for any deposit they pay. Check that the company named on the receipt is the mover you meant to hire. The full charges belong in the mover's agreement, with its Not to Exceed Price.

Is renting a truck cheaper than hiring Bay Area movers?

Usually, on paper. A 20-foot rental truck costs $39.95–$40.00 a day plus $0.69–$2.49 per mile in town, by published rental prices, against $720–$1,800 for movers on a baseline 2-bedroom move. But you load it, drive it over the hills and find somewhere to park it, so weigh how much do movers cost Bay Area households against a long day of your own work.

How far ahead should you book Bay Area movers?

Give yourself several weeks. The mover needs time for a visual inspection and must deliver your agreement at least three days before the move, and San Francisco parking signs take at least 5 business days to arrange. Summer is the busiest season, when how much do movers cost Bay Area households is at its highest, so book earliest for a date from May through September.
